scientific_scope_status: For a fixed universal Turing machine U, the source proposes a fixed finite canonical phase space, homogeneous quartic K with computable coefficients, homogeneous quadratic observable O and effective exact initial encoding w->z_w. For every rational 0<eta<1, an effectively chosen rational epsilon>0 yields H_eta(z)=||z||^2/2+epsilon K(z)/(1+||z||^2)^2 with global Hessian bounds (1-eta)I <= Hess H <= (1+eta)I. The flow is complete and radius-conserving. All encoded inputs have common radius 1<R^2<2 and common energy R^2/2. Along them O lies in [0,1] and tends to the halting bit: nonhalting inputs always have O<=64/1025<1/8; halting inputs eventually have O>=3/4. This is a complete source-reported constructive proof candidate relative to one published simulator theorem, not independently established correctness or originality.
